tags.label: Historical reasoning
tags.description: Using time, context, evidence, cause/effect, and continuity/change to explain the past.

tags.label: Source and evidence reasoning
tags.description: Interpreting sources, assessing credibility, distinguishing fact/opinion, supporting claims.

tags.label: Geographic reasoning
tags.description: Using maps, regions, places, movement, and spatial relationships to explain human activity.

tags.label: Civic judgment
tags.description: Reasoning about rights, laws, institutions, citizenship, democracy, and public life.

tags.label: Economic reasoning
tags.description: Reasoning about resources, production, consumption, trade, incentives, and systems.

tags.label: Perspective-taking
tags.description: Understanding different actors, interests, identities, and points of view.

tags.label: Cause/effect reasoning
tags.description: Explaining short-term and long-term causes, effects, and unintended consequences.

tags.label: Continuity/change reasoning
tags.description: Identifying persistence, transformation, reform, rupture, and historical patterns.

tags.label: Conundrum reasoning
tags.description: Reasoning through tradeoffs, dilemmas, competing values, and judgment under uncertainty.

tags.label: Narrative reconstruction
tags.description: Reconstructing events, actors, motives, decisions, and consequences into coherent explanations.

tags.label: Map-story reasoning
tags.description: Connecting geography, movement, place, conflict, and historical sequence.
